verdict.summary: I read the HLD, LLD and decisions against all seven inputs and the 14 checks. All 14 HLD sections, all LLD template sections and the nine ADRs are present. FR-001 to FR-033 and NFR-001 to NFR-011 keep their PRD ids, and MVP/R2 priorities, open questions Q-007/Q-008/Q-009/Q-015 and ISS-001 are carried as assumptions or risks. The HLD, LLD and ADRs agree on technology, ownership and the sync/async split, and the diagrams look syntactically valid. Only minor gaps remain; the main one is that the live `requests.md` was not in the output directory, so I could not check the request list directly.

verdict.summary: I checked all 14 points against the HLD v1, LLD v1, the user stories and the single contract. Both documents carry 'Based on: architecture v1' and have every template section in order. All 13 HLD entities have a table with the HLD's owner and classification, and the two extra tables have ent- ids and name the entity they serve. All 10 rel- ids have a subsection. The contract is OpenAPI 3.0.3 at version 1.0.0 with 50 operations, matching the Contracts table and integration-specs section 2. It has an unauthenticated /health, an Error schema used on every 4xx/5xx, security on every operation and pagination on every list. Every story except US-026 is cited by an operation. I found no blocking gaps, only the minor ones listed.

verdict.summary: I checked both files against the HLD, scope, estimate, backlog, clarifications and the earlier Phase 3B documents. I found no blocking gap. RSK-001 to RSK-010 keep the HLD ids and meanings, with RSK-001 re-scored and the reason given. All 38 scores, ratings and heat-map cells check out and the totals (1 Critical, 9 High, 25 Medium, 3 Low) are right. Every High and Critical risk is in section 4. The dependency rows cover the HLD's rel-001 to rel-010, every container and external system, and the platform services. Scope DEP-001 to DEP-006 keep their ids, and the open Q-007, Q-008, Q-009 and Q-015 each have a dependency row and a risk. The flowchart matches the rows and its syntax is valid. The build order marks the critical path, the estimate's 7–13 weeks against the 16 available is covered by RSK-011 and RSK-012, and no vendor SLA or price is invented.
